The image displays a close-up of a soybean leaf with numerous small, irregularly shaped lesions. The lesions are dark brown and appear somewhat raised. There is also evidence of chlorosis, or yellowing, of the leaf tissue surrounding the spots. A key feature is the presence of what look like tiny tan-colored pustules or blisters in the center of the lesions, particularly on the underside. The spots have begun to merge into larger necrotic areas. Comparing these observations to the knowledge base, the description for `Bacterial_Pustule` is the strongest match: "Symptoms begin as small, light green spots (not water-soaked) with raised centers... Light-colored pustules (blisters) often develop in the center of lesions, especially on the undersides of leaves. The lesions can grow together into large irregular brown areas." The description also helps differentiate it from similar diseases, noting the lack of water-soaking and the presence of tiny tan bumps, which aligns with the visual evidence.
